subject: Urgent: FastCommerce hosted API — p95/p99 latency & token/s drop
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir@fastcommerce.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>
Cc: FastCommerce Platform Team <ops@fastcommerce.com>
Date: 2027-12-04T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Sudden p95/p99 spikes & token/s halved since 08:45

Elliot —

We're seeing a severe degradation in the Hosted API responses for our checkout-recommendation pipeline starting ~08:45 PST. p95 and p99 have jumped ~2-3x and our observed token-per-second rate is roughly 40–50% of the baseline. This is causing timeouts in our edge service and retry storms.

Attached is a short CSV with measured token/sec samples from a subset of requests (token-rate-sample.csv). We rolled no changes on our side this morning. Can you confirm if anything was pushed that could affect token throughput (quantization or kernel changes)? This is impacting live traffic.

—Samir
Samir Khan
Head of Platform, FastCommerce

To: Samir Khan <samir@fastcommerce.com>
Cc: FastCommerce Platform Team <ops@fastcommerce.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-12-04T09:24:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 spikes & token/s halved since 08:45

Samir — thanks for the data and the heads-up. I'm escalating this to engineering and patching in our on-call.

Immediate next steps from our side:
- I'm opening a priority investigation ticket and CC'ing our inference team.
- Can you confirm whether the degraded requests share long-context prompts (~>2048 tokens) or are short prompts? That will help triage whether it's a kernel/long-sequence path.
- We will target a mitigation within the hour (rollback or per-account routing) and will follow up with an ETA shortly.

I'll keep you posted in this thread. Apologies for the disruption.

—Elliot

Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-12-04T09:35:00-08:00
Subject: FASTCOMMERCE ESCALATION: hosted-api p99/p95 + token/s drop — please triage

Team —

FastCommerce (FC-2027-119) reports a hard regression in p95/p99 and token-per-second starting ~08:45 PST. They attached token-rate-sample.csv showing consistent ~50% drop in token/s across several request shapes.

Context: Yesterday evening we deployed a staged change to the kernel selector and rolled quantization profile v2.1 for several quant-friendly models in Hosted API (small subset, canary regions). This may have affected throughput on certain kernels.

Can inference/runtime investigate:
- Whether the kernel selector is choosing a slower kernel path for quantized weights for longer sequences.
- Any correlation with quant profile v2.1 or fallback kernel code paths.
- Proposal for immediate mitigation (rollback quant profile for model/redwood/gptxx-16q in us-east-1 OR force routing FC requests to a non-quant variant).

Please treat as P0 — customer is live and experiencing timeouts.

—Elliot
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2027-12-04T11:10:12-08:00
Subject: Re: FASTCOMMERCE ESCALATION: hosted-api p99/p95 + token/s drop — initial analysis

TL;DR: profiling shows token/s drop tied to kernel selector + quant profile v2.1 for long-context flows.

What I ran quickly: workload replay from 08:30–09:10 on canary infra (us-east-1). Observations:
- For sequences > 1.5k tokens the kernel selector picked a fallback GEMM kernel path for quantized matrices that is ~2.1x slower than the path used for the float variant.
- The quant profile v2.1 added a new packed layout that the selector prefers; however the fused kernels we ship for that layout are not optimized for long context steps (they favor memory locality for short sequences).
- Net effect: p95/p99 latency rises and token/s drops ~40–55% on those requests — matches customer CSV.

Attachments: kernel-rollout-report.pdf (profiling traces + heatmaps) and trace links (see related_links).

Immediate mitigations (ranked):
1) Roll back quant profile v2.1 for redwood/gptxx-16q in Hosted API us-east-1 (fastest, high confidence).
2) Force routing for FastCommerce to redwood/gptxx-16 (float) variant for their API key (no rollback) — medium effort but isolates one customer.
3) Hotfix: enable fallback to older GEMM kernel for long-seq paths when quantized layout is selected — engineering work, ETA ~48–72 hours.

I recommend option #1 as immediate step, followed by #3 to restore the perf characteristics we expect for long sequences.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Principal Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, elliot.price@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2027-12-04T12:05:36-08:00
Subject: Re: FASTCOMMERCE ESCALATION: hosted-api p99/p95 + token/s drop — rollback plan

Agreed with Laura's analysis. Quick operational plan I can run with infra:
1) Execute rollback of quant profile v2.1 for model redwood/gptxx-16q in Hosted API (us-east-1) — command and runbook attached (rollback-runbook.txt). Estimated impact window: 30–60 minutes; no model artifact change, just revert active quant profile mapping.
2) If rollback is not acceptable, we can create a per-key routing rule to route FastCommerce's API key to redwood/gptxx-16 (float) while we implement the kernel fix. ETA for routing change: ~20 minutes.

I'll start the rollback as soon as I have green light from leadership (cost/credits note below).

Operational note: rollback reduces our token-cost improvements for affected hosts; expected unit cost delta is ~+15% while quant profile is off.

—Jonas
From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir@fastcommerce.com>
Cc: FastCommerce Platform Team <ops@fastcommerce.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2027-12-04T12:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 spikes & token/s halved since 08:45

Samir — quick update: engineering traced the regression to a quant/profile + kernel selector interaction for long contexts. We plan to roll back the quant profile for redwood/gptxx-16q in us-east-1 now. Jonas estimates 30–60 minutes for the change and we will monitor your key for improvement.

Options for you if you'd prefer: immediate per-key routing to a float variant (ETA ~20 minutes) or wait for the rollback (ETA up to 60 minutes). Which do you prefer?

We will also follow with a brief post-mortem and an exec summary. Again, apologies for the disruption — we know this is customer-impacting and are prioritizing it.

—Elliot
